product_from_film: Agora-2 is presented as a simulated world where people and AI agents can act together.
explains_well: Labels and a four-human/sixteen-agent diagram make the shared-world idea concrete.
unclear: The film does not demonstrate learning quality or how the proposed wider industries would use it.
scenario: Humans and agents share a game-like environment to study interaction and coordination.
product_clear_basis: 9–10s explains agents taking actions; 12s adds humans in the same simulated world.

scenes.action: A person uses an old computer; simple angular animated figures replace the desk. A television-style frame carries Superintelligence, then Agora-2 appears between metallic disks.
scenes.design: Retro computer imagery, low-poly figures, blue-orange gradients.
scenes.purpose: Frame the announcement in a longer computing story.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–9s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Text defines the simulated world over a glowing grid. A dungeon scene labels agents and players; a monitor wall follows, then four humans and sixteen agents flank one game screen.
scenes.design: Blue light points, brown isometric game tiles, small role labels.
scenes.purpose: Explain shared participation and stated capacity.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 9–22s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Abstract metallic objects accompany a shared-experience statement. Game screens and a dungeon action scene illustrate studying interaction and coordination.
scenes.design: Blue fields alternate with monitor wall and game imagery.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 22–32s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A capability statement becomes industry words over a blue tunnel: robotics, autonomous driving, defense, energy and cybersecurity are legible samples.
scenes.design: Small serif labels against radiating blue detail and occasional colored artifacts.
scenes.purpose: Broaden the claim beyond the game example.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 32–42s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A try-today card and odyssey.systems appear, followed by a long dark Odyssey logo sequence with colored glints before settling.
scenes.design: Blue CTA field, dark textured final field and restrained wordmark.
scenes.purpose: Give a destination and close the identity.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 42–57.125s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: Computing-history imagery leads to a shared-world definition, game example, participant count, wider claims and CTA.
A person at an old computer watches geometric shapes; no modern product function is visible in 0–2s.
The product is defined at 9–12s. Research users are implied by studying AI interaction at 25–27s, not named directly.
Metallic objects change orientation and game characters occupy different positions; radiating backgrounds and scaling layouts support spectacle. Exact paths are unresolved.
The screen wall links individual game views to the participant diagram. Specific cuts and effects between 1 fps samples remain uncertain.
Brown game textures contrast with saturated blue grids and polished abstract objects; the last card is dark and grain-like.
Centered explanatory sentences carry the meaning. Small agent labels add detail, while several industry words are tiny against busy rays.
Voice delivery is unverified.
Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Old-computer footage, simple geometry, game-like screens and metallic graphics are mixed; origin and generation methods are unknown.
Source duration 57.125 s; Watch metadata 1920 × 1080. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: The written definition and four-plus-sixteen diagram explain the core concept silently; actual learning behavior stays abstract.
The central screen between participant groups is easy to locate. The later small industry labels compete with bright radial texture.
The core definition gets several seconds. The industry list moves quickly and introduces broad new uses without examples.
categories.experiment: Replace three industry labels with one actual interaction outcome.

categories.finding: The superintelligence opening is broader than the game demonstration can prove. The ending provides a try link but no measured learning result.
Retro computing and futuristic blue scenes appear intended to create a sense of progress; this is an interpretation only.
categories.reason: No viewer response or validated listening.

categories.finding: The same game-like world recurs through the explanation. Abstract objects and wider industries interrupt that concrete example.
The film claims up to 20 combined participants and shows labels plus a four/sixteen diagram. Capacity and learning effects are not independently tested.
Dungeon scenes and participant roles give specificity; generic blue tunnels and metallic shapes could serve many AI announcements.
Definition, shared game and participant diagram add distinct facts. The long 45–57s logo ending adds little explanation.
For Tin multi-agent workflows, show named roles surrounding one shared campaign state, then one action and its consequence.
categories.experiment: Use a three-role workflow diagram with one visible shared output, not a broad industry montage.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Translate a participant-count claim into labeled groups around one shared screen.
try: For Tin agent coordination, place three role labels around one campaign and show how a review action changes the shared output.
For a technical announcement, pair a one-sentence definition with one annotated result and hold both before adding wider use cases.
lessons.avoid: Broad industry promises without a visible example and a long logo ending after the CTA.
lessons.open: Actual model behavior, capacity, learning results, sound and exact motion remain unverified.

comparison.story: Retro computation → shared-world definition → game and participant count → industry claims → try link.
comparison.motion: Changing graphic scale/orientation and game states; only sampled state changes checked.
comparison.sound: No validated listening; voice, music, effects and sync unknown.
comparison.texture: Retro footage, game tiles, metallic objects and blue grids; provenance unknown.
comparison.lesson: A count diagram can make an abstract multi-agent claim understandable.
